SpecContent.description: The nine PRD sections one Spec carries (DR-PS-07): the lightweight product requirements document of CONTEXT.md. Every section is free text; the name alone is required.

further_notes.description: Anything else worth keeping beside the PRD.

out_of_scope.description: What this Spec deliberately does not deliver.

user_stories.description: The behaviour claims, one `US` bullet per line.

SpecContentState.description: The closed content-version vocabulary on the wire (DR-PS-08).

SpecExecutionState.description: The closed Spec execution vocabulary on the wire (DR-PS-12), tracked separately from every content version.

SpecRecord.description: The Spec record as every client sees it: the Project it belongs to, the number that Project minted, the execution tracked separately from content, and the Plan it belongs to once planned.

name.description: The Spec's name, from the current content.

number.description: The number this Project minted for this Spec; rendered with the Project's code, for example `CORE-S1`.

plan_id.description: The Plan this Spec belongs to once planned; `None` while unplanned (DR-PS-06).

project_id.description: The Project this Spec belongs to.

version.description: The aggregate version, for optimistic mutation checks.

SpecVersionRecord.description: One Spec content version as every client sees it: the PRD exactly as it stood when the version was minted or last drafted. Approved and superseded versions never change again, and superseded ones stay readable so Ticket pins resolve (DR-PS-11).

number.description: The version's number; the first content is one and every material change mints the next.

description: Response payload for the `spec.get` query: the Spec and every content version beside it, so prior versions stay queryable for diffing and for Ticket pins.
title: SpecGetResponse
